name: Measure the stated numeric target, then improve it under a keep-if-better rule
summary: When a task states a numeric goal for its finished work, such as a speedup, a latency, a cost, or a distance to a reference, measure it with a fixed harness and repeated runs, and never finish while it is unmet or unmeasured. Once the acceptance check passes, try one improvement at a time, and keep one only when the acceptance check still passes and the metric improves beyond the measured spread; otherwise restore the last passing workspace.

trigger.detail: Code finds every number in the instruction with its sentence; one Jev request per task judges, per number, whether it is a measured goal's threshold, its direction, its quantity, and what it is measured against (questions/metric-target.json). No phrase list picks a number.

output.detail: A measurement with its spread from a frozen harness (provided, or written by one Luna session from the goal and the workspace's file names), compared with the threshold; control.finish holds a done finish while the target is unmet or unmeasured, and control.optimize keeps or restores each round's change by the acceptance check and the metric.

source_tasks.how: Fable 5.1's passing runs measured the distance to reference logits and kept only option sets that reduced it.
Fable 5.1's passing runs measured the pipeline's latency with a fault harness before and after each change.
Fable 5.1's passing runs scored each change against a threshold table built from a proxy for the hidden metric.
Fable 5.1's passing runs timed the kernel against the reference, kept a backup, and restored it after a slower variant.
Fable 5.1's passing runs measured the job's run time against its budget; a failing run never measured it.
Fable 5.1's passing runs measured the routing cost with the provided checker and kept only improvements.

admission.record: Not admitted. Built behind two switches, metric_target and optimize, absent from every manifest. Measured offline on the 61 tasks with retained Coder One or Microluna trials, less the eleven mapped tasks: with the frozen wording Jev held the right target first on 14 of the 19 tasks that state one, but also held a target on 30 of 42 tasks that state none, 29 of them the harness's own time allowance; one wording change, measured in-sample, cut the false positives to 1 and the right first target to 11. Admission needs matched mini-task runs on tasks other than the source tasks, then a pinned family.
